messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High throttle events observed for prod/redwood-api (severity: page) -- rule: autoscale_throttle_rate > 0.5 for 3m
Priya (oncall): acked. I'm seeing a spike in pending_queue depth and tokens/sec per instance. Customers reporting 429s.
Jorge: copying logs now. which cluster?
Priya (oncall): hosted-us-east-1, pool 'shared-gen2'. tokens/sec per pod jumped from ~2k to 9k avg over last 2 min. pending_queue per pod > 120. autoscaler didn't kick until after 5m.
Kai: looking at the scaler metrics — it uses queue_depth threshold of 80 for scale up and cool-down 4m. With sudden token bursts that's too slow.
Rebecca (PM): customer impact? any accounts hit hard?
Priya (oncall): initial alert correlates with increased throttle_count; partial customer-facing errors for 3rd-party integration. Not full outage but degraded.
Jorge: fetching containers with high CPU: `kubectl get pods -l app=redwood-api -o wide` shows 6 pods saturated.
Priya (oncall): I manually increased desired replicas to 12 via console to relieve queue. Doing it now.
incident-bot: Deploy/scale event: manual_scale by Priya (oncall) -> replicas=12 at 1763301265
Kai: after scale, pending_queue normalized to ~30 within 90s, throttle_count trending down. Good.
Jorge: saving the spike graphs: https://grafana.company/redwood/graph?panelId=22&from=1763301000&to=1763301400
Priya (oncall): root cause looks like a traffic burst from queued background jobs + synchronous API clients. Autoscaler policy didn't consider tokens/sec per pod, only queue depth and cpu. We need a more direct signal.
Rebecca (PM): timeline for customers? need brief for CS.
Priya (oncall): Impact window ~ 1763301200-1763301320 (~2m with elevated 429s). Affected: a small subset of high-throughput integrations.
Kai: immediate mitigation notes: 1) reduce scale cooldown to 90s for this pool 2) add a tokens/sec per pod threshold for scale-up (tokens/sec > 5k for 1m) 3) alert for sustained throttle_rate > 0.2 across >2 pods for 3m.
Jorge: Agree. Also add an automated 'burst' mode: temporarily increase max replicas by +50% for 10m on sudden tokens/sec spike to avoid manual scale.
Priya (oncall): I'll apply temporary alert tweaks and dashboard tiles now.
Priya (oncall): Editing alert in Datadog:
```
- name: Autoscale tokens/sec surge
  query: avg(last_1m):avg:custom.redwood.tokens_per_pod{env:prod,pool:shared-gen2} by {pod} > 5000
  conditions: 1m duration
  severity: warn
```
Priya (oncall): And throttle alert: `sum:custom.redwood.throttle_count{env:prod,pool:shared-gen2} by {pod} > 5` for 3m -> page at severity=page.
Kai: Also create a Grafana panel that shows tokens/sec, pending_queue, and throttle_count stacked per pod for quick diagnosis. Add a heatmap for per-model KV cache pressure.
Jorge: pushed a quick dashboard: dashboards/ops/autoscale-short-term-spike (shared link)
Priya (oncall): Updated runbook snippet: when receivers see throttle page -> check tokens/sec and pending_queue, if tokens/sec spike => scale to min(max, current*2) and reduce cooldown to 90s. If CPU also saturated, escalate to eng-runtime.
Priya (oncall): runbook change added: https://confluence.company/runbooks/autoscale#tokens-spike (edit by Priya)
Rebecca (PM): Good. Can we also add a customer-facing blurb for CS about mitigation and ETA?
Priya (oncall): yep. Will draft: "We observed short-lived throttling on hosted API in us-east-1; mitigated by scaling and alert tuning; root cause: unexpected burst pattern. No action required from customers."
Jorge: For the post-incident follow-up (PIF): recommend tuning policy to use both tokens/sec and queue depth, reduce cooldowns, and implement burst-mode. Assign owners?
Priya (oncall): owner: Kai for autoscaler changes, Jorge for dashboards/alert copies, Rebecca to coordinate CS comms. I'll file the incident and include metrics.
Kai: I'll open a PR to infra-config with new autoscaler policy and test in staging: reduce cooldown, add tokens/sec metric based scaler, and burst-cap.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-43, severity=minor, owner=Priya (oncall)
Priya (oncall): Handoff to next oncall in 30m. Leaving notes in the incident.
next-oncall: ack received. I'll monitor for 1h and validate the new alert thresholds don't spike false positives.
Jorge: FYI, we should add a synthetic load test that simulates queued bursts and verify autoscaler response.
Priya (oncall): Agreed. I'll add that to the PIF action items.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: ALERT RESOLVED: autoscale_throttle_rate back to normal. Closing page at 1763301960
Priya (oncall): filing postmortem with the timeline and proposed config changes now.
Rebecca (PM): Thanks team — please add SLO impact estimate to the postmortem and mark customers notified if CS calls in. :thumbsup:
